Design notes for reviewers and later tickets:
- Span attributes the projection reads: spanStart (ISO), role (worker|orchestrator|reviewer|other; default worker when scoped to an attempt, else other), handle (stream identity), waitKind on wait_ms (queue|build_test|blocked|review|human_approval). Host adapters should send role and handle. - Sprint totals use one membership rule for everything (the attempt's plan revision; non-attempt spans by their scope.sprintId, else the ticket's sprint). Sprint waits are summed over tickets (ticket-ms) plus the checkpoint wait. A ticket whose sprint id changed by adoption gets no readiness (lead time missing), rather than an invented window.
- Readiness is derived in the service only where records show it (sprint activation and acceptance of every dependency). Otherwise lead time and waitBeforeDispatch are missing.
- Failed/canceled end times come from the event log; the row's updated_at (later rewritten by supersession or reconciliation) is only a fallback for runs imported without their local log.
- Spans scoped to an attempt count as its effort from the claim to the end of its review or reconciliation, so reviewer work after submit is the attempt's overhead. Span time outside that window is reported as outsideWindowMs, not counted.
- Delta/cumulative active_ms has no place in time and is listed as not_an_interval (not counted here).

outputs.summary: Adds a pure timing projection and its run feed, in commit e1f1165 on space-DM-172. projectTiming (src/core/space/timing.ts, helpers timingIntervals.ts and timingActivity.ts) takes server lifecycle events plus host/agent active_ms and wait_ms span events (spanStart, else observedAt minus the value, to observedAt) and returns classified segments and totals per attempt, ticket, sprint and run as of a cutoff. Claim-to-submit is attempt_elapsed only; active time is only where the attempt worker's activity spans cover it. Classes: active, queue (ready and unclaimed, awaiting reconciliation), build_test, blocked (run paused, host-reported), review (submitted, undecided), human_approval (sprint checkpoint, retry grant, host prompt), unknown (reason after_last_signal or no_activity_evidence). Inside an attempt: activity > host wait > pause > unknown. There is no waste class. Missing stops end at the run end, else the cutoff (open). An expired lease ends at its deadline, or at the takeover that expired it. Duplicates and out-of-order input are ordered, deduplicated (the first delivery of an observation id wins) and listed in anomalies. Nothing is negative or counted after the cutoff. Every number is a TimingQuantity (src/shared/domain/timing.ts) with a distinct kind type, unit, aggregation (single/union/sum), state (observed/estimated/partial/missing), coverage and open flag. A missing value is null and covers 0. Effort is summed over streams (source+actor+handle; without a handle, worker spans are keyed by attempt and other roles by role). It is reported beside the in-flight and active wall-clock unions and the sprint/run elapsed windows. Orchestrator, reviewer and other overhead is listed byRole and as overhead. Nested inclusive usage is not counted twice. Failed, rejected, canceled, expired and superseded attempts keep their elapsed time, effort and unknown time (effortByOutcome, with unreported counts). Carried-forward attempts are listed and not counted.
